subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should OpenClaw repair the Telegram SOCKS proxy failure through a shared scheme-aware proxy helper now, and should that happen by repairing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84582 or by replacing it?
rationale: The source path is plausible, but the repair changes compatibility-sensitive shared proxy behavior and the open candidate lacks enough live proof and route coverage for automation to choose the final contract alone.

options.title: Repair Shared Proxy Handling
options.body: Require a scheme-aware shared helper that covers explicit and env SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS modes, preserves HTTP proxy endpoint defaults, and includes live Telegram or equivalent SOCKS proof.

options.title: Accept Explicit-Only Scope
options.body: Land a narrower explicit-proxy fix while explicitly owning the env proxy gap and compatibility follow-up.

options.title: Defer Pending Live Repro
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for redacted current-release SOCKS5 diagnostics before accepting any proxy contract change.

recommendation.title: Repair Shared Proxy Handling
recommendation.body: Require a scheme-aware shared helper that covers explicit and env SOCKS/HTTP/HTTPS modes, preserves HTTP proxy endpoint defaults, and includes live Telegram or equivalent SOCKS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current evidence crosses Telegram transport and the shared Undici proxy helper, both areas with recent steipete history.
